question: A network engineer must restore the running configuration on a Cisco Nexus 5000 Series Switch to an existing snapshot called `stable1`. The restore procedure should proceed only if no errors occur. Which configuration should be used to accomplish this goal?
options: rollback checkpoint stable1 best-effort running-config best-effort
rollback checkpoint stable1 best-effort running-config atomic
theory: Restoring a saved checkpoint with rollback running-config checkpoint supports three trigger types, and because the requirement is that the restore proceed only if no errors occur, the atomic keyword is required — NX-OS's default mode that treats the entire rollback as a single all-or-nothing transaction and aborts immediately, applying nothing, if any single line fails to reapply. Best-effort would apply everything it can while ignoring failures, which does not satisfy a strict no-errors requirement. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 6 — Configuration Rollback Trigger Types)
